summary: Piecewise-linear keyframe interpolator. Given an input value a2, walks an array of segments (7 floats each: input-min, input-max, inverse range, output-min, output-max) at this+116, finds the active segment, interpolates the output, and, when the value actually changed (compared against last value this+68), fans the result out to every callback target in the listener array this+108. Out-of-range inputs clamp to the first or last segment endpoint.

operations.description: Guard on the listener array at this+108; if null the whole update is skipped.
Read segment count v3 from this+112 and initialize the segment index v4 to 0.
Only iterate when the segment count v3 is greater than zero.
Scan the segment array at this+116, stepping 7 floats per segment, while a2 exceeds the current segment's input-min (i[0]).
When a2 is within the current segment (a2 <= input-max i[1]), this segment is the active one.
Change detection: skip callbacks entirely when the last value this+68 already equals a2.
Record the new input value a2 into the last-value field this+68.
Linear interpolation: v10 = (a2 - input-min) * inverse-range i[2] * (output-max i[4] - output-min i[3]) + output-min i[3].
Invoke sub_551210(entry, v10) once per listener: iterate the this+104 listener-count entries of the array at this+108.
After exhausting every segment (++v4 == v3), a2 sits past the last segment's input-max; clamp to the final segment's output-max i[4].
Clamp guard: only emit the endpoint callback when last value this+68 differs from i[1] (last segment input-max).
Clamp path: set this+68 = i[1] and call sub_551210(entry, i[4]) for every listener.
Safety bail: return early if the running index v4 reaches or passes the segment count mid-scan.
Below-first-segment clamp after the scan loop ends with a2 <= the first segment's input-min: set last value this+68 to *i (first input-min) when it differs.
Below-first-segment clamp path: call sub_551210(entry, i[3]) with the first segment's output-min for every listener.
